messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Deploy pipelines failing across multiple repos. Root cause suspected: GitHub Actions + package registry errors. Error spike detected at 18:13 UTC. Auto-page sent to on-call.
alex: saw the alert, looking now. which pipelines are failing?
incident-bot: failing workflows: infra/hotfix, web/release, api/hotfix-runner. Errors: `error fetching package` and `503 Service Unavailable` from `npm.pkg.github.com` and `github.com` API timeouts.
maria: I'm on pager. already on the call with devon. tagging infra. @infra can you confirm if our runners are healthy?
infra: runners are green from our side. we see failed fetches to external endpoints in the runner logs. not internal disk/CPU issues.
devon: grabbing logs from the failing GH Actions job:
```
Run npm ci
npm ERR! code E503
npm ERR! 503 Service Unavailable - GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@redwood-internal/infra-utils
Error: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN npm.pkg.github.com
```
alex: that looks like DNS/HTTP errors to GitHub package registry. GitHub status page?
incident-bot: https://www.githubstatus.com incident: "Partial outage - Actions and Package Registry experiencing elevated error rates" (link)
samantha: customer impact: hotfix builds and deploy pipelines are blocked. we have one customer-facing incident already live (INC-2345). if hotfix can't ship we might miss SLA. need status page update.\npm: (reaction :eyes:)
alex: mitigation brainstorm: 1) promote last successful artifact (we publish built artifacts to S3/artifact-store) and manually deploy; 2) attempt to run builds using mirror registry (jsdelivr/unpkg doesn't host private packages) — not possible for private packages; 3) vendor patch in repo (risky); 4) fallback to staging canary artifacts.
maria: we should prefer manual deploy from artifact-store — fastest and least risk. is there a recent successful artifact for the hotfix?
devon: yes: s3://redwood-artifacts/web/hotfix/2026-03-15-1710.tar.gz built 2 hours ago. It contains the compiled bundles and server binary.
deploy-bot: queued manual deploy job: `deploy --artifact s3://redwood-artifacts/web/hotfix/2026-03-15-1710.tar.gz --env prod --force` (blocked: requires CI signature verification from GitHub Actions)
alex: blocking detail: our deploy pipeline has a step that verifies commit signing via a GitHub Actions artifact signature. because Actions is down, verification fails. we need a way to bypass verification for incident deploys.
infra: we can temporarily allow deploys that use an explicit incident token and require two owner approvals in the console. i can open a bypass for this incident and roll audit log entries.
maria: do it. create a console override and post the exact command. also we need PM and security signoff. @pm can you approve?\npm: (reaction :thumbsup:)\npm: (This reaction is a leftover debug)\npm is not a person; ignore.\npm: ???\npm: sorry wrong channel, ignore
pm: (system silence)\npm: ha
pm: (end)\npm:\npm
nate: pm here. I approve emergency override for prod deploys using the incident token. Security: will you and infra add a ticket for audit and rotate keys after?
infra: yes. creating bypass: `console override create --incident 1839506789 --allow-deploy --approvals 2 --expires 60m`
infra: bypass created. audit id: OVERRIDE-8921.
alex: proceeding with manual deploy:
```
# fetch artifact locally
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/web/hotfix/2026-03-15-1710.tar.gz /tmp/hotfix.tar.gz
# deploy
rcli deploy --artifact /tmp/hotfix.tar.gz --env prod --incident-override OVERRIDE-8921
```
devon: running now. logs show deploy step `pushing to cluster` succeeded. preflight checks passed.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: release v2026.3.15-hotfix promoted to prod at 18:23 UTC. (:+1:)
samantha: updating customers: "We've applied an emergency hotfix deploy; customer-impacting issue should be mitigated. Root cause: third-party GitHub Actions / Package Registry outage preventing builds. Working with GitHub for full restoration." I'll post to status.redwood.ai now.
alex: open support ticket with GitHub? we should also include our runner logs and the audit id.
maria: ticket opened: https://support.github.com/ticket/12345678 (internal link). github support PR triage says they're investigating and routing to SRE team.
alex: any other services affected? monitoring shows error spikes in deploy metrics only. runtime is stable.
samantha: CS: a few enterprise customers pinged earlier; I replied that we're deploying a mitigation and will follow up with postmortem.\npm: (reaction :pray:)
maria: on-call handoff in 10m to devon. I'll stay until deploy confirmed for all regions, then handoff.
devon: I'll take night on-call after that. keep me in loop.
ate: Nate is not on this thread.
alex: next steps: 1) infra to revoke OVERRIDE-8921 after verification and rotate any incident tokens; 2) eng-sre to collect full timeline and logs for postmortem; 3) PM/CS to update customers with ETA from GitHub and follow-up; 4) consider removing mandatory GH Actions signature dependency for emergency deploys or provide an alternative internal signature mechanism.
infra: will revoke override in 30m and file rotation tasks. ticket created: SCHED-3341.
maria: handing off to devon now — I'm stepping offline in 5m but will monitor Slack for urgent pings.
devon: ack, taking over. I confirm deploy is serving traffic for eu/us/apac. will watch errors for next hour.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation applied; hotfix deployed via artifact-store bypass at 18:23 UTC. GitHub status still shows degraded. Monitoring will continue.
samantha: closing loop with customers and noting rollback plan if any regressions.
alex: thanks all. we'll do a full incident review tomorrow. please add any missed items to the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
